items.prompt: An array never changes; answer 10^5 queries "what is the sum of nums[l..r]?".
items.why: Many arbitrary range sums on a static array → build prefix sums once and answer each query with one subtraction.

items.prompt: Count the contiguous subarrays whose sum equals k; the array contains negative numbers.
items.why: Negatives break the shrink rule of a window → prefix sums + a hash map counting earlier prefixes equal to prefix − k.

items.prompt: All values are positive. Find the length of the shortest contiguous subarray whose sum is at least target.
items.why: Positive values make the window sum monotone → grow and shrink a dynamic window in O(n) time and O(1) space.

items.prompt: Apply 10^5 operations "add v to every element in positions l..r", then print the final array.
items.why: Range updates read once at the end → a difference array (D[l] += v, D[r+1] −= v), then one prefix-sum pass.

items.prompt: A matrix is fixed; answer many queries for the sum of a sub-rectangle.
items.why: 2-D prefix sums → every rectangle sum is 4 lookups (inclusion–exclusion).

items.prompt: In a binary array, find the longest contiguous subarray with as many 0s as 1s.
items.why: Count 0 as −1, then it's the longest zero-sum subarray → map each prefix balance to its FIRST index.

items.prompt: In a sorted array, find two numbers that add up to a target.
items.why: A pair of elements, not a range, in sorted order → move two pointers inward from both ends.

items.prompt: Return the maximum sum of any k consecutive elements.
items.why: A fixed size k → slide a running sum: O(1) extra space. Prefix sums work too but store an extra array.
